samples.summary: No test drives DurableLossWatch's throw-guards, though an unguarded throw there unmounts every collaborative editor
samples.evidence:
`DurableLossWatch` is rendered unconditionally by `CollabDocumentProvider` for every collaborative document (collab-document-provider.tsx:308). It carries three defences added by this diff: the doc-like-stub guard (`typeof doc.subscribe !== 'function' || typeof doc.getKey !== 'function'`, line 258), the `watch()` try/catch around each `doc.subscribe(...)` — justified in the comment at lines 260-267 with "`subscribe` does not merely ignore an event name it does not know — it *throws* ... A throw out of a passive effect propagates through render and takes the whole editor subtree with it" — and the try/catch around each `unsubscribe()` in the cleanup (lines 300-310).

Nothing exercises any of them. In `packages/frontend/src/components/__tests__/collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx` the mocked `doc.subscribe` (lines 55-65) always records and returns a function; it never throws for an unknown event name, and the mocked `doc` always has both `subscribe` and `getKey`. In `packages/frontend/src/components/durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx` `fakeDoc()` (lines ~/`subscribe: (type, cb) => {...}`) likewise never throws, and `mockDoc` is only ever `undefined` or a full fake — which exercises the `!doc` early return but not the stub guard. I grepped `packages/frontend` for tests that make `subscribe` throw (`Unsupported event type`, `subscribe.*throw`, `mockImplementation(() => { throw`) and found none touching this component.

So removing or inverting any of these three guards leaves the whole suite green, while on a pinned `@yorkie-js/react` that does not know `local-changes-dropped`/`persist-disabled` the result is a blank editor rather than a chip that merely loses its certainty — exactly the outcome the comment says the guard exists to prevent.
searchedFor: read durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx fakeDoc() and the mockDoc lifecycle

samples.summary: The lapse-reason mapping is asserted by no test; every tooltip test hand-supplies the value it is meant to derive
samples.evidence:
`CollabDocumentProvider` computes which `DurabilityLapse` to publish at lines 291-299 (`unsupported` / `not-permitted` / `not-enabled` / fall-through `another-tab`). The design requirement quoted in `sync-status-tooltip.ts:20-24` is that the tooltip "must name which case applies", so this ternary chain is the thing that decides whether the user is told the truth.

No test asserts it. `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx` calls `tooltipFor(..., lapse)` with literals (lines 640-690) and, for the wiring cases, renders `DurabilityLapseScope` with hand-supplied lapses (lines ~712-755) — the provider is not in the tree at all. `src/components/__tests__/collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx` asserts `mounted`, `clientKey`, `locks.held` and `subscribers`, never the published lapse; I grepped `packages/frontend` for `'another-tab'`, `not-enabled`, `unsupported'` and `useDurabilityLapse` and the only test hits are the hand-supplied ones in the chip suite.

Consequence if the chain is wrong: the chip confidently states a false cause — e.g. the fall-through means any non-durable document that is supported, permitted and enabled is reported as "open in another tab", including the `pdf-` exclusion, with nothing to catch it.

samples.summary: belongsToAnotherUser — the filter that stops orphan collection deleting another account's rows — has no test
samples.evidence:
`orphanSnapshotKeys()` filters with `!this.belongsToAnotherUser(docKey)` (line 1253), and `belongsToAnotherUser` parses the `wb:{deviceSecret}:{userId}:` segment out of the store key with a regex (line 1273). The only orphan test is `wafflebase-doc-store-atomicity.test.ts` "is collected rather than living forever out of reach", which seeds `doc-a` — a key that matches the regex not at all, so it lands on the default `false` branch. No test seeds an orphan under `pk/wb:secret:other-user:sheet-x/sheet-x` to prove it is skipped, and none proves this user's own `wb:secret:user-1:...` orphan is still collected.

If the regex over-matched (e.g. capturing the device secret as the user id, which the group ordering makes easy to get wrong), every orphan would be classed as another account's and orphan collection would silently stop — a permanent quota leak holding document content, which is precisely the failure the surrounding comment says the sweep exists to prevent. Nothing in the suite would notice.
searchedFor: read wafflebase-doc-store-atomicity.test.ts 'an entry that predates the header rule'

samples.summary: The navigateRef-out-of-deps decision has no test, so a regression re-runs the whole housekeeping effect on every in-app navigation
samples.evidence:
`OfflineRuntime` holds `navigate` in a ref specifically so it is not an effect dependency (lines 55-65), with the comment naming the cost of regressing it: "a new database handle, the thirty-day sweep again, the archive listing again, and a title fetch per archive" on every navigation that leaves `PrivateRoute` mounted — and noting "The toast id dedupes what the user sees, which is exactly why the repetition would go unnoticed."

`offline-runtime.test.tsx` mocks `react-router-dom` with `useNavigate: () => navigate`, returning one stable `vi.fn()` forever, so the unstable-identity case the ref exists for can never arise in the suite. No test rerenders with a new `navigate` identity and asserts `constructed.length` / `collectStale` call counts stayed at one. Impact is contained (duplicate IndexedDB handles, repeat sweeps and per-archive fetches, invisible to the user by the author's own reasoning) rather than data-affecting.
searchedFor: read packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.test.tsx (react-router-dom mock and all rerender usage)

samples.summary: The keepArchives branch of dropAllForUser is reached by no caller and no test
samples.evidence: `dropAllForUser(userId, { keepArchives })` (line 1085, branch at 1123) and its passthrough `eraseOfflineData(store, userId, { keepArchives })` (offline-erase.ts:29). Grepping `packages/frontend` for `keepArchives` finds only those three sites — no caller ever passes `true`, and no test in `offline-erase.test.ts` or `wafflebase-doc-store-archive.test.ts` sets it. The comment at 1116 attributes it to "a session the server expired", but this diff makes that path erase nothing at all (`eraseLocalData: "none"` in auth.ts), so the branch is both dead and unexercised.

samples.summary: The volatile device-secret fallback (localStorage refused) is untested
samples.evidence: `deviceSecret()` catches a storage failure and falls back to a per-session `volatileSecret` (lines 147-153). `durable-session.test.ts` covers the happy path ("keeps the same key across reloads of this device", "is not derivable") via `resetDeviceSecretForTest`, but never stubs `localStorage.getItem/setItem` to throw — grepping for `volatileSecret` finds only the implementation. If the fallback regressed (e.g. minting a new secret per call), the client key would differ between the election and the mount within one session; nothing would catch it. Contained because this only occurs in browsers that refuse storage, where the feature is largely unavailable anyway.
searchedFor: Grep for Storage.prototype mocks in durable-session.test.ts

samples.summary: The legacy bare-string parse in pendingErases()/deniedIds() is untested
samples.evidence: Both `pendingErases()` (~line 283) and `deniedIds()` (~line 200) fall back to treating a non-JSON stored value as a single id, and `pendingErases` documents this as the pre-set on-disk shape that "must not have its owed erase dropped by the upgrade". `offline-erase.test.ts` only ever produces these values through the module's own writers, which always emit JSON arrays — no case writes a bare string into `wafflebase-offline-erase-pending` or `wafflebase-offline-denied` and then asserts the erase is still owed / the write still refused. A regression here silently drops an owed erase on an upgraded device, leaving another account's documents on a shared disk; low likelihood, and the window closes once the value is rewritten.

samples.summary: The 'not the default' control renders the mocked provider, so it asserts only the context default
samples.evidence: `CollabDocumentProvider` is replaced wholesale by `vi.mock('@/components/collab-document-provider', ...)` at the top of the file, so `render(<CollabDocumentProvider docKey="sheet-7" />)` in the second case exercises the probe, not the real component — it reduces to `expect(createContext(true) default).toBe true`. As a control for the first case that is acceptable and not vacuous in intent, but it does not establish what its name suggests ("it is the route saying so") about the real provider; the first case already carries the whole claim.

verdict.reason: I located all six references to DurableLossWatch; it is rendered only by collab-document-provider.tsx:308 and by durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx. The three defences are real (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:258 stub guard, :269-278 watch() try/catch, :297-307 unsubscribe try/catch). Neither test suite drives them: durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx's fakeDoc() (lines 70-86) always exposes getKey+subscribe and its subscribe never throws and returns a well-behaved unsubscriber, with mockDoc only ever undefined (exercising the !doc return at :254) or a full fake; collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx's mocked doc (lines 53-66) likewise always has both members and never throws on an unknown event name — its two watch cases (lines 388-432) assert only positive subscription/latching. I searched wider for a counterexample: repo-wide greps for 'Unsupported event type', 'subscribe.*throw', 'throw new YorkieError', and the component's two console.warn strings turn up nothing outside the component itself; every other suite mocking useDocument (tests/components/sync-status/*, tests/app/files/pdf-collab*, document-detail-lakehouse-tab, user-presence, lakehouse-view) does not mount DurableLossWatch with a durable context. The one suite that supplies a doc lacking subscribe/getKey (collab-document-provider.test.tsx:48-60) mocks useQuery to return no identity, so no DurableYorkieProvider mounts and the effect returns at :254 on !durable before the stub guard at :258 is reached — so even that does not pin the guard. All three guards could be deleted with the suite staying green, and under this lens that is a changed behavior whose failure (an unguarded throw out of a passive effect unmounting every collaborative editor subtree) is user-visible, i.e. major.

finding.summary: The new `watch()` try/catch around `doc.subscribe` — the entire point of this delta's provider change — has no test where `subscribe` throws
finding.evidence: The delta wraps both subscriptions because `subscribe` throws `YorkieError(ErrInvalidArgument, 'Unsupported event type')` on SDK versions that don't know these events, and a throw out of the effect would take down the editor subtree. Both suites that exercise `DurableLossWatch` use fake docs whose `subscribe` accepts any event name and never throws: `durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx:74-81` (`subscribe: (type, cb) => { handlers.set(...); return () => ... }`) and `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:55-65`. So the guarded path is never executed — deleting the try/catch (or catching the wrong thing) leaves every test green while the real failure it exists for (the whole collaborative document unmounting on an older SDK) ships undetected. There is also no test that when the first subscription throws the second is still attempted, and that the already-registered unsubscribers are still collected/cleaned up.

verdict.reason: The try/catch in `watch()` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:268-296) and the cleanup's try/catch (:297-307) exist because `doc.subscribe` throws on SDK versions that don't know these event names. No test in the repository ever makes `subscribe` throw. The only two suites that mount `DurableLossWatch` use fake docs whose `subscribe` accepts any event name and returns an unsubscriber: durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx:70-86 and collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:53-66. I also checked every other place `CollabDocumentProvider` (which mounts the watch) is rendered in tests — collab-document-provider.test.tsx (stub has no `subscribe`, so the effect exits at the typeof guard at :258-259 and never reaches `watch()`), collab-document-provider-identity.test.tsx:31, the sync-status suites, document-detail-lakehouse-tab.test.tsx:133, pdf-collab.test.tsx:44, shared-document-durability.test.tsx:37 — none throws from `subscribe`, and none mounts the watch under a durable context. Repo-wide greps for `DurableLossWatch`, the two event names, `YorkieError|ErrInvalidArgument`, and throwing-subscribe patterns turn up no counterexample. Removing the guard (or catching only one of the two subscriptions) leaves every test green while the real failure it exists for — a throw out of a passive effect unmounting the whole collaborative-document subtree on an older SDK pin — ships undetected. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a missing test over a behavior whose failure breaks a path a user takes: major.

finding.summary: `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` changed from swallow-and-return-0 to propagating the failure, and no unit test pins the new contract
finding.evidence: The delta removes the `catch { console.warn(...); return 0; }` from `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` so the caller's recovery gate can distinguish 'reconciled' from 'failed'. `packages/frontend/src/lib/offline-erase.test.ts` (the `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` describe block, lines ~460-551) has no case where `storedDocumentIds`/`purgeDocument` fails; every assertion is on a resolved count. Nothing fails if someone restores the swallow — and if it is restored, the runtime gate opens on a reconcile that never happened, which is exactly the harm (offering an archive from a workspace the user was removed from) the change exists to prevent. The runtime-level test 'offers nothing back when the purge itself failed' mocks `@/lib/offline-erase` wholesale (offline-runtime.test.tsx:20-28), so it cannot cover the real function. Also untested: that `store.close()` in the `finally` still runs on the throwing path.

verdict.reason: The finding's evidence checks out. offline-erase.ts:452-494 defines purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments with try/finally and no catch, and its doc comment (:443-450) makes throw-on-failure an explicit contract the caller's recovery gate depends on. The matching test block, offline-erase.test.ts:457-552, has six cases and every one asserts a resolved count; the file contains no rejects/toThrow for this function, and its only mockRejectedValue uses (176, 364, 380, 405, 431) target dropAllForUser in the erase/logout blocks. Restoring a `catch { return 0 }` would fail nothing. I searched beyond the reviewer's paths: every file importing @/lib/offline-erase (durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx:36, documents.test.ts:5, workspaces.test.ts:14, tests/api/auth.test.ts:87) vi.mocks the module and none mentions this function; api/workspaces.ts:151 references it only in prose; offline-runtime.test.tsx:15-28 stubs the whole module so its failure-path test at :248-260 exercises a vi.fn, not the real function; no test stubs storedDocumentIds or rejects purgeDocument; and a glob for offline-related e2e files turned up nothing. No counterexample exists. In-lane as a missing test over a changed behavior, and major because a restored swallow silently opens the recovery gate on a reconcile that never happened — offering back an archive from a workspace the user was removed from — with no test turning red.
